In Europe (and many other locations) governments (or more like towns and cities) use to have designated areas for markets, some every day fixed hours, some weekly, some free, some with paid stalls, and combinations of those. It was actually normal to have a giant paved void in the middle of a city for the market, usually around the church.

It gradually became a great way to extract more and more money from the citizens using a lengthy list of excuses. Billing per meter, business registrations, service cost, cleaning, licenses, etc etc

It was normalized but there is nothing normal about it. Normal would be for a government to use taxes to organize things for the citizens. They can just build a mall and set a low rent for each shop, do inspections, monitor complaints. You are not providing a service to the citizens by maximizing their exploitation.

Not that you should but you can set up an online marketplace in 20 minutes. Any forum software will do it. If you want it to be fast and full of high resolution media the citizen will have to pay something like $0.001 for hosting.

You can go full retard with a blend of top notch nepotism and bureaucratic inefficiency and make a platform that costs whole dollars per citizen.

Do the full paper trail where the goods come from, digital ID, encrypt and lock everything behind court orders, automatic taxes if you sell more than $30k, tax foreign merchants.

You will have an inevitable explosion of economic activity and a huge surge in purchase power.

It is completely obvious.

I found a word for what we are doing in stead, I'm calling it COLONIALISM.
